title: 第69章 秦川的被动技能第70章 信息差的商业应用
lines: 入谷第十天，秦川无意间触发了一项他从未意识到的“被动技能”。
事情发生在藏书阁。那天下午他在翻阅一本名为《中界风物志》的杂书，书中记载了中界各大宗门的建宗历史、传承脉络和历代代表人物。这本书的作者是百草谷第三代谷主的一位好友，文笔严谨，内容详实，在注释部分收录了大量关于各宗门的秘闻轶事——虽说是“轶事”，但秦川注意到每条注释都有明确的出处和采访对象，更像是一本严谨的风物志而不是小说。
他翻到关于凌云宗的章节时，目光忽然停住了。
书里记载了凌云宗第三代掌门的成名之战——以一人之力镇压南疆异兽潮，一剑斩断三座山峰，其中一座山体被斩开后，露出了一段天然形成的石钟乳洞穴，洞壁上刻满了上古铭文。这些铭文的拓片后来被送往上界刑天殿鉴定，鉴定结果是一段万年前终焉之战残存的历史记录。拓片现藏于凌云宗祖师堂，非掌门不得翻阅。
秦川将这一段与上次凌云宗来青山村的态度拼在一起——周鹤年长老为什么对青山村既畏惧又执着？不只是因为老陆的剑，更是因为凌云宗拥有终焉之战的历史记录。他们知道九尊是什么人，知道青山村镇压着什么。所以他们既不敢冒犯，又想从青山村获取更多信息。
旁边有个正在查资料的丹堂弟子，正在低声抱怨自己的研究瓶颈——几味同为火属性的药材放在一起炼制时，不知道应该用什么顺序才能让灵气流转最顺畅。同行的另一个弟子随口说了句“回去问师父吧”。
秦川合上书，对那个丹堂弟子说：“你可以试试换顺序。先放性温的，再放性燥的。温能缓冲燥，让灵气流转时不至于冲断经脉。”
那弟子愣了一下，抬头看他：“你怎么知道？”
秦川没有解释，只是说他刚才翻的一本书里有这个说法。其实那本书和炼丹毫无关系——是他在翻阅《经络归经总论》时看到一个关于“气机缓急”的注脚，说人体经脉承受灵气冲击时需要一个缓冲区间，否则会逆流。他把这个原理套在了炼丹上。
那弟子道了声谢，将信将疑地走了。
当天傍晚，那弟子又跑回来，满脸兴奋地说按他的顺序炼丹果然成功了，火属性的几味药融得比平时更顺，炼出的丹药品质提高了一成多。秦川还没来得及反应，消息已经传开了——那个圣女带回来的凡人，不光会治病，还懂炼丹。
短短两天内，开始有丹堂和针堂的弟子主动来找秦川请教。问的问题五花八门，但秦川注意到一个规律——所有他能“解答”的问题，本质上都不是他“懂”这个领域，而是他在翻阅其他书籍时看到过相关的原理。他只是比这些专精于一门的弟子多翻了几本不同领域的书，然后将不同领域之间的信息进行关联和迁移。
这就是他在青山村积累的“信息差”技能的升级版——青山村时是观察人物的行为模式和背景进行推演，百草谷则变成了在大量专业典籍之间建立跨领域连接。学科壁垒越森严，跨领域信息差的价值就越大。
一个针堂弟子说他在给凡人施针时总是把握不好深度，不知该用几成力。秦川想起李神医教他的第一课——凡人经脉没有灵气，所以针不能靠灵力感知，要靠手感。针尖碰到筋膜和骨膜时的阻力不同，用这个判断深度。这是在地球上任何一个中医学院的基础教材里都会写的内容，但在这个一切靠灵力感知的世界里，没有人教过这个。
苏木槿很快注意到了这个现象。她站在藏书阁门口，看着被几个弟子围住的秦川，表情有几分意外，又有几分了然。
“你在青山村也是这样的吗？”秦川从人群中脱身之后，她问。
“在青山村我只是劈柴的。”
“但你到了百草谷才短短十天，就有弟子开始找你请教了。这不是碰巧——是你有一种在平凡的事务里发现不平凡关系的能力。”苏木槿认真地看着他，“青山村的劈柴，到了百草谷就变成了——在这里的任何一本书里，只要你看过了，就能找到和其他书的关联。”
“这个能力在青山村不值一提。”秦川说。
“为什么？”
“因为青山村的书架上，只有劈柴。”他合上手中的典籍，“但百草谷有几千本书。书越多，这个能力就越有用。”
苏木槿没有说话。她低头看着秦川手里的医典，似乎在思考这个“被动技能”的逻辑——不是修为，不是灵根，不是任何这个世界的修炼体系可以衡量的东西。只是一种纯粹的、跨领域的观察力和连接力。
秦川将书放回书架。他心里清楚，这项能力不是天生就有的——是他在青山村那一个多月里，每天劈柴、观察、记信息、找规律，慢慢磨出来的。老陆让他劈柴，劈的不是木头，是观察力。每一块柴都有不同的纹理、硬度、湿度，每一斧下去都要调整角度和力度。一个多月劈下来，他的眼睛和手，已经习惯了在混乱中找到规律。
如今这双眼睛正在以另一种方式“劈柴”——百草谷就是一座堆满木材的林子，问题是他不知道哪块木材里藏着什么纹路，但他知道只要劈下去，总会找到规律。
content_en:
On the tenth day after entering the valley, Qin Chuan accidentally triggered a "passive skill" that he had never realized.
It happened in the library. That afternoon he was flipping through a miscellaneous book called "Zhongjie Fengwu Zhi", which recorded the history, inheritance and representative figures of the major sects in the Middle Realm. The author of this book is a good friend of the third-generation owner of Baicao Valley. The writing is rigorous and the content is detailed. The annotations include a large number of secret anecdotes about each sect. Although it is called "anecdote", Qin Chuan noticed that each annotation has a clear source and interviewee. It is more like a rigorous chronicle than a novel.
When he turned to the chapter about Lingyun Sect, his eyes suddenly stopped.
The book records the famous battle of the third generation head of Lingyun Sect - suppressing the tide of alien beasts in southern Xinjiang with one man's power, cutting off three mountain peaks with one sword. After one of the mountains was cut open, a naturally formed stalactite cave was exposed, with ancient inscriptions carved on the cave wall. The rubbings of these inscriptions were later sent to the Xingtian Palace in the upper realm for appraisal. The appraisal result was a historical record of the remaining battle of the Final Battle ten thousand years ago. The rubbings are now hidden in the Lingyun Sect's Ancestral Hall, and no one but the head master is allowed to read them.
Qin Chuan put this paragraph together with the Lingyun Sect's attitude last time when they came to Qingshan Village - why is Elder Zhou Henian both afraid and persistent towards Qingshan Village? Not only because of Lao Lu's sword, but also because Lingyun Sect has the historical record of the final battle. They know who Jiuzun is and what they are suppressing in Qingshan Village. So they didn't dare to offend, but they also wanted to get more information from Qingshan Village.
Next to him, there was a Dantang disciple who was looking up information, and was complaining in a low voice about his research bottleneck - when several medicinal materials with the same fire attribute were put together for refining, he didn't know what order should be used to allow the smoothest flow of spiritual energy. Another disciple who was traveling with him casually said, "Go back and ask Master."
Qin Chuan closed the book and said to the disciple of the Alchemy Hall: "You can try changing the order. Put the warm ones first, then the dry ones. Warmth can buffer the dryness, so that the spiritual energy will not interrupt the meridians when it circulates."
The disciple was stunned for a moment and looked up at him: "How do you know?"
Qin Chuan did not explain, but said that this statement was found in a book he just read. In fact, that book had nothing to do with alchemy—it was when he was flipping through the "General Theory of Meridian Guidance" that he saw a footnote about "the urgency of Qi movement", saying that the human body's meridians need a buffer zone when they bear the impact of spiritual energy, otherwise they will flow backward. He applied this principle to alchemy.
The disciple thanked him and left doubtfully.
In the evening of the same day, the disciple came back again and said with excitement that the elixir refining according to his order was indeed successful. The fire-attribute medicine blended more smoothly than usual, and the quality of the elixir refined improved by more than 10%. Before Qin Chuan had time to react, the news had already spread - the mortal brought back by the saint could not only cure diseases, but also know how to make elixirs.
In just two days, disciples from the Alchemy Hall and the Needle Hall began to come to Qin Chuan for advice. The questions asked were all kinds of, but Qin Chuan noticed a pattern - all the questions he could "answer" were not essentially that he "understood" the field, but that he had seen relevant principles when reading other books. He just read a few more books in different fields than these disciples who specialized in one field, and then related and transferred the information between different fields.
This is an upgraded version of the "information gap" skill he accumulated in Qingshan Village - in Qingshan Village, he observed the characters' behavior patterns and backgrounds to deduce, while in Baicao Valley, it became a matter of establishing cross-field connections between a large number of professional classics. The tighter the disciplinary barriers, the greater the value of cross-field information gaps.
A disciple of the Acupuncture Hall said that he always failed to grasp the depth when applying acupuncture to ordinary people and did not know how much force to use. Qin Chuan remembered the first lesson Dr. Li taught him - mortal meridians do not have aura, so needles cannot be sensed by spiritual power, but by feel. The needle tip has different resistance when it hits the fascia and periosteum. Use this to judge the depth. This is something that is written in the basic textbooks of any Chinese medicine school on the planet, but in this world where everything relies on spiritual perception, no one has ever taught this.
Su Mujin quickly noticed this phenomenon. She stood at the door of the library and looked at Qin Chuan, who was surrounded by several disciples. Her expression was a bit surprised, but also a bit understanding.
"Is this the same for you in Qingshan Village?" Qin Chuan asked after he got away from the crowd.
"In Qingshan Village, I was just a woodcutter."
"But it has only been ten days since you arrived at Baicao Valley that disciples have started to ask you for advice. This is not a coincidence - it is because you have the ability to find extraordinary relationships in ordinary things." Su Muzhen looked at him seriously, "Chopping firewood in Qingshan Village has become - in any book here, as long as you read it, you can find connections with other books."
"This ability is not worth mentioning in Qingshan Village." Qin Chuan said.
"Why?"
"Because the bookshelves in Qingshan Village only have chopped firewood." He closed the classics in his hand, "but there are thousands of books in Baicao Valley. The more books there are, the more useful this ability will be."
Su Muxin said nothing. She looked down at the medical book in Qin Chuan's hand, seeming to be thinking about the logic of this "passive skill" - not cultivation, not spiritual roots, not something that can be measured by any cultivation system in this world. Just pure, cross-disciplinary observation and connection.
Qin Chuan put the book back on the bookshelf. He knew in his heart that this ability was not something he was born with - it was slowly developed during the more than a month he spent in Qingshan Village, chopping firewood, observing, memorizing information, and looking for patterns every day. Lao Lu asked him to chop wood. What he chopped was not wood, but observation. Each piece of firewood has different texture, hardness, and moisture, and the angle and strength must be adjusted every time the ax is struck.
